intro: A wish or a request from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive: quería que vinieras.
p.quería.consejo: It is the imperfect of «querer». After «quería que», the next verb is also in the past.
p.esperaba.consejo: With the meaning «to hope», it asks for the subjunctive after «que»: «esperaba que llegaras».
p.pidió.consejo: It is the past of «pedir»: the e of the verb becomes i. You say: «me pidió que llamara».
p.vinieras.consejo: It comes from «vinieron»: drop «-ron» and add «-ras». It is used after «quería que».
p.llamara.consejo: It comes from «llamaron»: «-ron» becomes «-ra». The ll sounds like y: ya-MA-ra.
p.terminara.consejo: A regular -ar verb: «terminaron» gives «terminara». After «querían que» it is the right form.
p.ayer.consejo: It speaks of the day that has passed, so the verb is in the past. It sounds a-YER.
p.cena.consejo: It is the noun for «cenar». The c sounds like th: THE-na.
p.postre.consejo: It is masculine: «el postre». The stress falls on the first syllable: POS-tre.
p.perdonar.consejo: It is a regular -ar verb. In «te perdono», the ending -o already says that «yo» speaks.
b1.titulo: The wish also travels to the past
b1.texto:
If the wish is from **today**, the verb goes in the present subjunctive:

- **Quiero** que **vengas**.

If the wish is from **yesterday**, both verbs go in the past:

- **Quería** que **vinieras**.
- Me **pidió** que **llamara**.

The second form is the **imperfect subjunctive**. It is used when the person changes: the one who wishes and the one who acts are different.
b2.f0.texto: Yesterday I wanted you to come to dinner.
b2.f1.texto: I wanted to go, but I had to work until late.
b2.f2.texto: My sister asked me to call you in the afternoon.
b2.f3.texto: I did not see your call until ten.
b2.f4.texto: I hoped you would arrive at least in time for dessert.
b2.f5.texto: My bosses wanted me to finish a report.
b2.f6.texto: Then I forgive you, but I want you to come to the next one.
b4.titulo: How the imperfect subjunctive is formed
b4.texto:
Start from the **ellos** form of the preterite, drop **-ron** and add **-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran**:

- hablaron → hablara, hablaras, hablara, habláramos, hablarais, hablaran
- vinieron → viniera, vinieras, viniera, viniéramos, vinierais, vinieran
- pidieron → pidiera, pidieras, pidiera, pidiéramos, pidierais, pidieran

The rule of two persons:

- Same subject → **infinitive**: Quería ir.
- Different subject → **que + imperfect subjunctive**: Quería que vinieras.

The present turns into the past: quiero que **vengas** → quería que **vinieras**.
b4.e0.texto: My mother wanted me to speak slowly.
b4.e1.texto: He asked me not to arrive late.
b4.e2.texto: We hoped that everyone would come.
b5.f0.texto: Every Sunday, grandmother laid the table with a cloth of blue flowers.
b5.f1.texto: She wanted everyone to sit near the window.
b5.f2.texto: From the oven came a sweet smell of cinnamon.
b5.f3.texto: The children waited in silence by the door.
b5.f4.texto: Nobody began to eat before her signal.
b5.f5.texto: She asked that nobody talk about work during the meal.
b5.f6.texto: Her soft voice filled the room like a warm blanket.
b5.f7.texto: My father told her stories of ships and faraway ports.
b5.f8.texto: We hoped the afternoon would last forever.
b5.f9.texto: Even today, the memory of that cinnamon fills my kitchen.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Vengas» is present subjunctive: it serves a wish from today.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes! The wish is from the past, so the second verb is too.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Vienes» is indicative: a wish does not allow it.
b6.pregunta: It is a wish from yesterday. Which verb follows?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Estudie» is present subjunctive; the wish is from the past.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Estudiaba» is indicative and does not work after «querían que».
b7.pregunta: They were two different people. Which form is missing?
b8.traduccion: He asked me to call you
b9.frase: Quería ____ a la cena, pero trabajé.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Well done: with a single subject the infinitive goes.
b9.o1.refuerzo: That would mean another person goes; here it is the same one.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Voy» is indicative and does not fit after a wish either.
b9.pregunta: The one who wants and the one who goes is the same person.
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Ayer» asks for the past, but «quiero» and «vengas» are present.
b10.o1.refuerzo: The second verb fails: after «quería que» comes «vinieras».
b10.o2.refuerzo: Correct: both verbs speak of yesterday.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I wanted you to come.»
b12.frase: Me pidió que te ____ por la tarde.
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Llamo» is present indicative: it does not work after «pidió que».
b12.o1.refuerzo: That's it! «Pidió» is in the past, so «llamara» is too.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Llame» is present subjunctive; here you need the past.
b12.pregunta: The request was yesterday. Which form is missing?
p.llegaras.consejo: From «llegaron»: drop «-ron», add «-ras». The ll sounds like y: ye-GA-ras.
p.jefes.consejo: Plural of «jefe». The j sounds like h: HE-fes. The feminine is «jefa».
p.querían.consejo: Imperfect of «querer» for ellos. After «querían que» the subjunctive follows.
p.perdono.consejo: From «perdonar», for yo. The ending -o already says that «yo» speaks.
p.vengas.consejo: Present subjunctive of «venir» for tú. It comes from «vengo»: vengo → vengas.
p.próxima.consejo: Feminine of «próximo». The x sounds like ks and the accent marks the stress: PROK-si-ma.
p.prometo.consejo: From «prometer», for yo. In «te lo prometo», «te» is to you and «lo» is what you promise.
p.llegara.consejo: From «llegaron»: «-ron» becomes «-ra». The ll sounds like y: ye-GA-ra.
p.esperábamos.consejo: Imperfect of «esperar» for nosotros. The accent falls on «RA»: es-pe-RA-ba-mos.
p.vinieran.consejo: From «vinieron»: «-ron» becomes «-ran». It is used after «esperábamos que».
p.ponía.consejo: Imperfect of «poner». «Poner la mesa» means to set the table. The accent separates i-a.
p.sentaran.consejo: From «sentaron»: «-ron» becomes «-ran». In «se sentaran», «se» goes with the verb.
p.salía.consejo: Imperfect of «salir». The accent on «í» separates the vowels: sa-LÍ-a.
p.esperaban.consejo: Imperfect of «esperar» for ellos. «Esperar» means both to wait and to hope.
p.empezaba.consejo: Imperfect of «empezar». The z sounds like th before a: em-pe-THA-ba.
p.pedía.consejo: Imperfect of «pedir». After «pedía que» the subjunctive follows: «pedía que hablara».
p.llenaba.consejo: Imperfect of «llenar». The ll sounds like y: ye-NA-ba. It comes from «lleno», full.
p.tibia.consejo: Feminine of «tibio». It agrees with «manta». The «ia» sounds as one beat: TI-bya.
p.contaba.consejo: Imperfect of «contar». It means to tell or to count. Here: to tell stories.
p.historias.consejo: Plural of «historia». It means stories and also history. The h is silent: is-TO-ryas.
p.barcos.consejo: Plural of «barco». The b and the v sound the same in Spanish, so write it carefully.
p.puertos.consejo: Plural of «puerto». Careful: «puerta» is a door, «puerto» is where ships dock.
p.lejanos.consejo: Masculine plural of «lejano». It comes from «lejos». The j sounds like h: le-HA-nos.
p.durara.consejo: From «duraron»: «-ron» becomes «-ra». «Durar» means to last or continue in time.
p.medicina.consejo: It is feminine: «la medicina». It also means a remedy. The c sounds like th: me-di-THI-na.
p.estudiara.consejo: From «estudiaron»: «-ron» becomes «-ra». It is used after «querían que».
